Arena row and ovalSides, ovalAxisRatio, ovalMajorFactor: measure at M3a-V2 (T-V2-42), panel at M6; M3 removes ovalCourt where it cannot fit, M14 fallback. @deck rows and stand-ins: measure at M3a-V2 (T-V2-47 >= 95 % in band), panel at M4; stand-ins close fixed: superseded by V11's deck row. Small tables and massing constants: measure at M6a and M6b (SP-V2-1 >= 40 % of rich manor plots admitting a court; T-V2-3, T-V2-9-12, T-V2-30), panel at M6; PorchKindRow entries written by the M3a-V2 seat. sunBias: panel at M6 then corpus. crypt.clearCm, crypt.freeboardCm, vaultClampCm: measure by T-V2-36 and T-V2-28 from V04's access draw landing, panel at U5. terrace.wallBandCm: measure at M3a-V2 (T-V2-51), panel at M4. viewBatchMs: measure at M6b (T-V2-22), V2 §6.2 fallbacks. Options massing.composed and fantasyShapes: no entry (fixed: an option). Keys and laws (roleKeys, classFamily, MassingGrowthRow keep and anchor, axis, arcade, arrangement law): not calibratable, no entry.

V02-0210.statement: Elaboration: city band massing only (eager footprints with wings and heights). District band and finer before any click: the massing's roofscape (ridges, hips, valleys, cones, spires, cupola) drawn lazily per tile from model data (§8.5 lazy list); no composition, district band requests none. A neighbourhood click (II.4, V01), an outline close-up (V1-3.8.9: buildings inside centre-out) or a visible tile's request at neighbourhood band or finer under view: the pool runs compose(..., wings) per building centre-out from the click (or tile centre), each result a cache chunk with record current; tile worker re-rasters (DisplayDelta §8.9); a tile request sliced into batches of at most viewBatchMs (16 ms pool time, §12.7) when larger; tile draws the massing's roofscape until each batch lands. A building click from the neighbourhood band down: wings (if absent or stale), rooms, plan (V03), each recorded; at city and district bands a building click is the district's click (V1-3.8.1: close-up and wings rung) selecting the building without rooms or plan; a double-click reaches the plan at any band (V03 §4.5; J-S23.5).

V02-0211.statement: wings rung staleness (wingsInputs; J-V2.52): recorded inputs exactly a digest of the base wings (keys, roles, rings, heights, roofs), the main entrance (wing key, side, offset) and any entrance a secondary porch stands at, Building.massing, the composition.json slices read, and for the porch's space the plot's ring with the footprints of the plot's other buildings and yard parts within porch.depthM[1] + clearanceM of the main (and secondary) entrance; nothing else: a relet, household move, use change, access, sub-location, band drift, Works stage or material change leaves it current with no change marker (T-V2-21); a dossier event of items 18, 22, 31 reaches it only through those inputs. rooms rung stale: wingsInputs plus occupants' band row and value, household count (BCR-V2-13), the class's programme hall row, its own slices.

V02-0212.statement: Canonical prior: an unstored composition has none to carry (pure function of the committed massing with draws keyed per wing key, so kept wings recompose exactly: least disruption by construction); a stored composition is re-matched inside the changing event (W8) and never stale (state edited). Re-rolls: regenerate rung wings advances #wings (dormer counts, kinds, porches re-draw; massing unchanged, T-V2-14); rung rooms advances #rooms (hall length, chapel); New random on the building's plot or block re-derives the massing (S11) with the plot's reroll (§6.1).

V02-0213.statement: Concerns (next append-only u16 ids): massing (geometry concern, non-rerollable by salt, attempt cap 3, readers S11 and every operator re-deriving S11 on a plot; keyed by the building's entity key with S11's stage id; creation indices 0 family and width and sunlit coins' base draws, 1 family lengths, sides, walk, 2 blocks, 3 towers, turret, template towers, 4 back range and M8b attached wings, 5 floors then tower storeys, 6 roofs and towers' flat tops, 7 cupola, 8 stepped tiers' count, shape, step, top, stair width, grade, shrine (no aspect), 9 tiers' heights in tier order; ovalCourt width at 0, semi-axis factor, axis ratio, seating depth at 1); compose.dormers, compose.porch (geometry, non-rerollable, attempt cap 0, keyed with #wings folded (§6.1 rung rule); index 2 x key + eave per dormer row, 0 porch, 1 secondary porch); compose.rooms (keyed with #wings and #rooms folded; 0 hall, 1 gate hall, 2 chapel).

V02-0214.statement: Draws in edits and mutations (stated once; J-V2.18): the designation mutator draws on siteplan.mutate: W1's family draw with creation index the causing event's seq and ordinal 0; W6's draws with index the event's seq and the new wing's key as ordinal; a setMassing family op draws exactly so (replayable); every other setMassing op and every setComposition op draws nothing (an omitted value takes the row's central value: range midpoint, heaviest weight; stochastically rounded count round-half-up of the central value); a W6 wing over a sealed void draws its access on V04's sewer key, never these streams; the bends draw nothing (deterministic), except a bend to a family op (tiers on a non-stepped building) draws as a family op; a stepped mutation's drawTiers takes its two streams on siteplan.mutate with the event's seq and ordinals nextWingKey (index-8 group) and nextWingKey + 1 (heights).

V02-0215.statement: Arithmetic: massing and composer use + - x / and sqrt only (§6.5) and dmath's cos and sin for regular polygon vertices (regularCourt, towers, half-round porch, §1.7 dmath); every result snaps by the placement rule; metre draws converted to integer cm before construction; facadeBays' valley reaches integer; the roofscape is view data in float64 under the renderer's CPU reference (§6.5 (9)). Order: candidates enumerated in a fixed geometric order (union ring order from its lowest vertex, then ranges in path order) before any weighted draw; weighted draws use §14's Rng weighted-pick helper. Stability: same state gives same massing and composition on every host (T-V2-13); a New random of a finer rung never changes a coarser one (§6.1); the elaboration cache can be dropped any time (§2.9).

V02-0216.statement: F-MASSING = V2 §3.5's M14 (rungs 0-3 per building, base rectangle last), M10's reverse-lattice steps on the same attempt counter; a failing template tower or attached wing dropped and reported, building kept; for stepped the ladder runs inside massStepped (TierFailure an attempt, then the single fallback, then the base rectangle). F-COMPOSE (per building at derivation, reported to the view report, counted by T-V2-18, never an error): (1) a failing dormer dropped; (2) a porch whose space fails takes the next feasible kind then none (secondary porch none); (3) a composer room the seed contract would refuse (outside its piece, or a vertex within attractCm of an unshared side) shortened once by 2 x attractCm away from the offender, then omitted (V03's A2 (11) places that role, S23-27); (4) any other stage-3 contract failure (a bug by construction) returns the identity composition (composed wings and towers one to one, no dormer, no porch, no room), which satisfies the contract, and files the building in the report; a porch meeting one of the building's own other wings takes (2)'s ladder narrowed first to the free part of its side.

V02-0217.statement: File g's base mechanisms are the coherence pass's (prosperity driver, siting profile, supply web, wall closure, ladder table); V2 §3.14 designs only their building part, citing g's item for the rest.

V02-0218.statement: Sunlight (item 102 (b)(d)(e)): (a) a building's shade casters are its base wings' prisms (ring from baseCm to eave; over its ring the roof's rise: gable or hip ridge prism, a tower's cone or spire only over its own ring); these are item 102's epoch casters (at an epoch §4.11 the previous epoch's buildings enter the daylight raster through them); no stage-3 wing is a generation-time caster (buildings never feed the term they are sited by); the composition (dormers, porches, cupola) never casts in the model; cross-volume: V06 §3.4 rasterises per wing, not one height per footprint. (b) The rich seek the sun at building scale: M5's sunlit choice (J-V2.38). (c) Over time: a wing added or raised at an epoch changes the next epoch's casters only; V06 owns the drift.

V02-0219.statement: Custom institutions (item 104; V11 §3.13): compose as the class DR24 resolves (archetype, category, tags, library fields or fallback; V08, V11 §3.13.2) through the ordinary chain; (a) landmarkLevel and economicWeight act through significance; (b) the ruined landmark (ruined-landmark -> generic-other) massed by its class's row then takes the ruined existence at its site (roof none; §2.8 decline states; V2 §5.1); (c) subsumption (item 104 (h)(5); item 108 source subsumption): the subsuming kind's template takes each subsumed kind's structures as extra slots (names by roleKeys, shares added to the compound's budget), nothing merged into one wing; (d) custom supply chains place members, never shapes.

V02-0220.statement: Split works-and-shop sites (item 105 (h); J-V2.54): one institution on two plots: the branchOf use's building composes by split.shop, the works building by split.works (V11 §2.3), each an ordinary building (composed, mutated, undone by W1-W9); a merge-back (clerk's or author's declaration, or V06's re-evaluation) is two designation mutations inside one event: the works plot toward the class's unsplit template family (shop structure added by W6 as a frontage slot) and the shop plot toward vacancy (base subtract steps), both in EditBase.mutations and reversed together (undo restores both byte for byte, T-V2-39).

V02-0221.statement: Ladders (item 108; J-V2.55): COUNT, QUARTER, GUILD members are ordinary buildings of the lesser class (LadderStepRow.memberClass) each by its own chain; a GUILD's hall composes as the hall family; a SIZE building composes as the greater class's family with sizeFactor in M10's budget (and σ's rank in step 3) so 'city granaries' are one compound of several stores; an upgrade keeps the existing building as member #1 (row arrangement kept: W1-W9; row -> compound: W3b); a demotion keeps the member nearest its demand and reverses added slots; as-built bytes return (T-V2-40).

V02-0222.statement: Dig floor (item 109 (j); V02 is its producer, read by V04's access draw): baseCm - Basement.floors x cellar.depthCm with a basement (raised crypt's floor for a raised one), else baseCm; baseCm includes a half basement's raise (half cellar's floor = datum less half the depth; BCR-V2-28); a building on a deck plot has no dig floor and never draws; a wing with on never draws; a quay on the bank (surfaceCm null) is ground and has one. Who digs: a building draws its access once when built (draw V04's C4-52; chance V11 §3.23.7 DigRule, SCC-22); a wing the mutator adds over a sealed void draws once for that wing (W6); a setMassing op draws nothing (a user declares addUndergroundAccess, item 66); a replacement building (new lineage) draws as new (J-V2.39).

V02-0223.statement: cryptSeedWings(b) (stated once; J-V2.92): for a building with template part names (BaseWing.partName, BCR-V3-13) the wings named chancel, else apse, else crossing; else for a stepped building its tier 0 (tier wing with no on); else the one storeyed ground wing (no on, not solid) of role main, range or cross whose ridge has the end with the largest world x (farthest east), ties by lowest key; else none (empty list: V03 places the crypt under the third of the region farthest from the main entrance, V03 3.7.4 step 1); returns wing keys; exported by @plat/plots beside massStepped; called by §2.6's basement function (BCR-V3-20 crypt ring; BCR-V2-28 lift and half raise on wings over the basement's ring); read by V03's crypt placement, T-V2-36, T-V2-53. The crypt is Basement.crypt (BCR-V3-20, derived by §2.6 from V11's crypt column); V02 owns the wet-ground lift and the half raise. After every basement re-derivation (setMassing commit step 3, a designation mutation, a terrain change) an always-class crypt (cathedral, great temple, a building a dossier crypt record binds to) is kept with no condition; a basement-class church keeps its drawn crypt while its class stays in the church family; a mutation out of that family drops it through re-derivation, contents to V03/V04's closure, never silently.

V02-0224.statement: Cathedral's crypt never refused (J-V2.46): ladder with no refusal rung: full crypt; half-sunk where the full floor would lie below the water table or the plot is low (wings over it raised by cellar.depthCm/2, BCR-V2-28, floor at datum less half depth); raised-choir crypt (Basement.kind raised) where even a half floor would lie below the water table or on a damp or flood plot: floor at max(lowest terrain sample under its ring, water table + crypt.freeboardCm), the ground storey of ground wings over the basement's ring lifted to clear the basement by crypt.clearCm (250 cm; the seed wings over a crypt-only basement; every ground wing over the whole inset V03 gives a crypt no stair reaches, V03 §3.7.4, S23R6-02), written by the basement step as those wings' Heights.baseCm with steps at the crypt ring's edge (V03 plans choir stairs, V3C-61 (4)). Inside a solid platform (V2C-68): seed wing a solid tier 0 of height >= crypt.clearCm + 100 cm: crypt inside tier 0 (floor as above, vault >= 100 cm under tier 0's top), no lift (stair 0 and stack keep heights); any other ground wing over the ring lifted as above; the lift applies only to a lower or storeyed tier 0 and then through rebaseStack. On a sky island the rim-slab vault is V05's form of the ladder. (e) Size and rank not V02's (cryptM2, rank via §2.6 with V11, BCR-V3-20). (f) Catacombs never V02's: no V02 path sources, moves, re-sources or shrinks one (item 109 (k)(2)(4)); V02's footprint and basement floor are an obstacle input to (k)(5)'s stagnation; a V02 demolition or replacement lifts that block; a crypt joins a catacomb only by V04's (3b) link.

V02-0225.statement: Siting-profile columns shaping a building (item 103): none save two: emits.smoke >= 2 adds one decorative stack per level above 1 to the row's hearths (forge, kiln, brewhouse, dyer's chimney; §8.10 drawn until a plan exists); needs.runningWater selects the water axis for the main slot (M2); every other column is S10b's and the solver's (V11 §2.3); materials texture and colour.

V02-0226.statement: A stepped building is reached only by name: a class whose designation template's composition key is one of V2 §3.15.4's rows (V11's specialisations, X17), a setMassing {family stepped} (or a tiers op bent to it) or a mutation toward such a row; no default, family, override or role row lists stepped (no-op pin, T-V2-50). One exported function decides the bytes (J-V2.80): M5 calls massStepped and the base outline builder calls the same massStepped from M3a (BCR-V2-39) with the same row, band, streams, so a pre-M6 stepped building keeps its bytes when stage 3 registers (T-V2-46); massStepped owns frame, band, draws, attempts, fallbacks; layTiers owns only the geometry and is what the tiers op, the mutator's anchored lay and V04's ruins call.

V02-0227.statement: massStepped(input, row, band, k) in order: (1) frontage frame (V2 §3.4 steps 1-2); (2) slotBand -> lo, hi, cap (stepped rows carry claimShare: claimShare x area(H) x sizeFactor); (3) ST0, infeasible -> step 6 reported steppedInfeasible; (4) for attempt a = 0, 1, 2 (massing cap 3): drawTiers on massing creation indices 8 and 9 (a = 0) or massing/attempt=a's 8 and 9; layTiers at scale 1; ST8; an accepted TierLay converted to wings and MassingRef (ST7 order and keys) and returned; a TierFailure reported with step and detail, next attempt; (5) attempts exhausted -> step 6; (6) the single fallback (ST8's construction), then if its checks fail the base outline rectangle in H (M14 rungs 2 and 3). storeys = class HeightsRow.storeyCm; pitch, parapetCm, plinthCm = M11's pitch rule, the family's parapet, §2.6's plinth.

V02-0228.statement: ST0 feasibility (M3 for stepped): at least draws n0 = count[0], d0 = insetM[0], sw0 = stairWidthM[0], ĝ = stairGrade[1] (steepest: least run), least heights h_k (solid solidHeightM[0] x taper^k, storeyed storeys.groundCm); least stair reserve r0 (axial (h0 + plinthCm)/ĝ, flights sw0 + stairClearM, internal 0); least front insets f_k, k = 1..n0-1 (axial max(d0, h_k/ĝ + landingM), flights max(d0, sw0 + stairClearM), internal d0); least top width t0 = tierMinSideM (flights max(tierMinSideM, h_{n0-1}/ĝ + landingM)). rect: Wmin = t0 + 2(n0-1)d0, Dmin = r0 + Σ f_k + (n0-1)d0 + tierMinSideM; feasible when W >= Wmin and D >= Dmin; Amin = Wmin x (Dmin - r0) + sw0 x r0. round or octagonal: least inradius ρ = tierMinSideM/2 + Σ max(d0, f_k); feasible when min(W, D - r0)/2 x cos(π/m) >= ρ (m side count: 8 or round bracket); Amin = m ρ² tan(π/m) + sw0 x r0; infeasible also when Amin > 1.1 x hi. Anchored mode (mutator W1): anchor's shorter side >= tierMinSideM + 2d0 and least reserve r0 of width sw0 fits inside H in front of the anchor's front side (none for internal).

V02-0229.statement: ST1 draws (drawTiers): on s8 in order n uniform on count's integers; shape by weights; d = U(insetM); top by weights; sw = U(stairWidthM); g = U(stairGrade); for a shrine top its floors (uniform integer in shrine.floors), U(shrine.insetShare), roof kind by shrine.roofs. On s9 per tier k in order: solid tier (every tier under solid all; tier 0 only under lower) heightCm_k = U(solidHeightM) x taper^k rounded to the cm, floors_k = 0; storeyed floors_k = max(1, floor(U(tierFloors) x taper^k + u)) (u a second uniform), heightCm_k = storeys.groundCm + (floors_k - 1) x storeys.upperCm (each stacked tier's first storey a principal one, J-V2.85), never a parapet here (ST4 adds it). No aspect drawn (J-V2.86). All drawn once; ST8's re-lays and anchored mode re-use them (a shrink never shifts a draw). V04 draws the same list on its ruin stream.

V02-0230.statement: ST2 tier 0 and stair reserve: reserve r at the front (-v side) of Rr: axial (heightCm0 + plinthCm)/g, flights sw + stairClearM, internal and none 0; the stack's own proportion (J-V2.86): W_need = t + 2(n-1)d, D_need = Σ d_k + (n-1)d + tierMinSideM (ST0's closed form at the drawn values), laid aspect = clamp(W_need / D_need, aspect cell); tier 0 in [0, W] x [r, D]: rect W0 = min(W, aspect x (D - r)) x scale, D0 = min(D - r, W0 / aspect), centred on u = W/2, front on v = r; round a regular ring with TowerShapeRow round side count, circumradius R0 = min(W, D - r)/2 x scale, centred, one side parallel to u nearest the front; octagon an 8-gon same circumradius and phase; every tier of a round or octagonal stack keeps tier 0's side count (concentric offsets vertex for vertex). D-front: under axial a round or octagonal ring's front chords within (sw + 2 x stairClearM)/2 of the centre line replaced by one straight edge (chord between the ring's crossings of u = c ± (sw + 2 x stairClearM)/2 on its front half). Anchored mode: tier 0 is the anchor as given (a kept range's four corners, extra vertices leaving with subtracted wings; or the tiers op's re-laid ring), reserve sought in front inside the region, else stair form falls back (never the ring). Flights: tier 0's front face >= (heightCm0 + plinthCm)/g + landingM else fallback.

V02-0231.statement: ST3 tiers above (J-V2.74): for k = 1..n-1 front inset d_k: axial max(d, heightCm_k/g + landingM), flights max(d, sw + stairClearM), internal and none d; rect: tier k's ring = tier k-1's corners moved inward by d on back and sides and d_k on the front; round or octagonal: concentric, inradius reduced by max(d, d_k) all round (regular), same side count, then D-front under axial; on = tier k-1; the stack ends at tier k-1 where tier k's shorter side (polygon: twice its inradius) would fall below tierMinSideM or, for flights, its front face below heightCm_k/g + landingM; truncated counts tiers not laid (reported tiersTruncated). Stair fallback: with fewer than two tiers laid, re-run from ST2 with the next form of input.forms (absent: the row's form then axial -> flights -> internal; internal only where tier 0 is storeyed; a round or octagonal stack skips flights; none only where input.forms names it (an edit's bend) and tier 0 solid); past the last form layTiers returns TierFailure {noSecondTier, ST3}; the form laid is TierLay.stairs.

V02-0232.statement: ST4 roofs and heights (J-V2.75): every tier but the top: lowerRoof flat (roof flat with parapetCm, ridgeCm = eaveCm, walkable terrace) or pent (hip rect, pyramid octagon, cone round, pitch p_k = min(pitch, pentShare x storeys.groundCm / d), ridgeCm = eaveCm + p_k x d: the band between the ring and the ring above, V2 §5.2 step 3's band facets); pent needs equal insets (internal or none form where every d_k = d; load check and tiers op bend). Top tier (whichever tier the lay ended on): flat and shrine top roof flat with parapetCm; roofed hip (rect) at the pitch rule's pitch, pyramid (octagon) or cone (round) at TowerShapeRow's pitch, ridge by M11's formulas. Each tier eaveCm = heightCm_k plus parapetCm on every flat-roofed tier solid or storeyed (so deckLevel subtracts exactly), Heights.floors = floors_k, solid where floors_k = 0. Shrine: top tier's ring moved inward by insetShare x its shorter side on every side (rect in a rect stack, regular ring otherwise), laid only where area >= 4 m² and each side >= 2 m else top becomes flat (shrineDropped); on = top tier; floors and roof as drawn; storeys groundCm then upperCm; role shrine.

V02-0233.statement: ST5 stairs: axial: width min(sw, tier k's straight front edge length); stair k the rect of that width centred on the centre line along v, reaching from tier k's front face toward the front by run_k = rise_k / g (rise_k = heightCm_k for k >= 1, heightCm0 + plinthCm for k = 0; re-read by rebaseStack); stair 0 on the ground in the reserve (no on), stair k >= 1 on tier k-1's front terrace (on = tier k-1), rest of the front inset a landing before its foot. Flights: stair k the rect of length run_k along u and width sw along v against tier k's front face, on the ground (k = 0) or tier k-1's terrace; stair 0's foot at the face's left end (seen from front) climbing +u; for k >= 1 the foot is the point of tier k's front face nearest stair k-1's head, moved along the face only as far as the flight needs, climbing toward the end with more room. Every stair role stair, solid, roof shed with high its ring side at the upper end, eaveCm 0, ridgeCm = rise_k. Internal: no stair wing, V03's cores climb inside (X18). None (sealed): no stair wing, no way up; a storeyed shrine or tier on it is reached by nothing and V03 flags W_TIER_UNREACHED.

V02-0234.statement: ST6 snap and validate (M13 for stepped): every ring snapped; every stair vertex lying on a tier ring's side inserted into that ring (§2.6 rule 1: stair 0's head vertices into tier 0's front side, stair k's into tier k's, a flight's back vertices into its face) so contact is exact and a carry keeps it; ground wings (tier 0, stair 0) tile; every wing with on inside the ring of its support (exact orient2d), boundary >= minEdge from that ring's except a stair whose foot lies on the terrace edge; wings standing on one wing pairwise interior-disjoint (stair k abuts tier k on shared vertices); each stair rise/run <= g x 1.01; stairChain connects the ground to the top terrace for axial and flights; a regular ring stays regular except its D-front edge; every wing >= 4 m², every side >= minEdge; failure returns TierFailure {check, ST6, detail}.

V02-0235.statement: ST7 order, keys, hint: keys 0..m-1 in the order tier 0, stair 0, tier 1, stair 1, ..., tier n-1, stair n-1, then the shrine (no stairs under internal or none); no tower, so canonical order holds; nextWingKey = m; massStepped writes MassingRef.family stepped, segments 1, row, grammar, entrance, stack (shape, stairs, lowerRoof, top, insetCm, grade, truncated). Hint: a solid tier 0 under axial or flights: stair 0's outer side (axial: the side at its foot; flights: its -v side), so the main entrance is the stair's foot and the plan roots at the first landing door (BCR-V2-41); a storeyed tier 0: tier 0's front side, the door on its free part (BCR-V2-38); under none: tier 0's front side, an entrance opening nothing (BCR-V2-41).

V02-0236.statement: ST8 size budget (M10 for stepped, inside massStepped): A = area of tier 0 ∪ stair 0, A_t tier 0's, A_s stair 0's; over 1.1 x min(hi, cap): where A_s >= min(hi, cap) the single fallback at once; else scale <- scale x sqrt((min(hi, cap) - A_s) / A_t) and layTiers re-runs once with the same draws (tiers may truncate; only tier 0's size moves the footprint); still over or a TierFailure: the next attempt, at the end the single fallback. Under 0.9 x lo: scale grows once by the least of sqrt(lo / A) and the largest factor keeping tier 0 and the reserve in Rr. Single fallback (no draw, so M3a and M6 builders agree): w = max(0.8 x wingWidthM[0], 3 m), L = clamp(min(hi, cap) / w, 1.2w, W), slab [u0 + (W - L)/2, u0 + (W + L)/2] x [v0, v0 + w] (single along the frontage), role main, roof flat with parapet, floors the template's least; MassingRef.family single, reported steppedFallback; failing M13's checks the base rectangle. A stepped row is never read on a deck (V2 §3.16's rows admit no stepped; family stepped there bends to single).

V02-0237.statement: rebaseStack (J-V2.81): every path re-basing a wing of a stacked building calls it for the whole building, never the per-wing step: S11's datum step, a setMassing commit, a tier height edit, §7.3 (a) 4's terrain operator (whenever any ground wing is on a changed sample), §7.4's warp and moveVertex, carry rule (2), the crypt lift, a deck's re-base. Steps: (1) ground wings by the terrain rule (BCR-V2-32's levelledGroundCm samples with BCR-V2-42's wall-side move, so a levelling re-bases through S11's datum step); a ground wing's user-edited baseCm (J-DET-24's kept fate) kept and carries the stack; (2) each wing with on in stack order (after its support, whatever the keys), baseCm = deckLevel of its support; (3) each stair's ridgeCm re-set to its true rise (stair 0 deckLevel(tier 0) - stair0.baseCm; stair k deckLevel(tier k) - deckLevel(tier k-1)); where it exceeds g x run x 1.1 it is kept and reported stairSteep; the run is never re-laid by the datum pass (J-V2.2: the massing owns every ring); (4) envelope: Building.heights.baseCm least baseCm of ground wings; eaveCm, ridgeCm maxima over non-tower wings of w.baseCm + w.eaveCm - baseCm and w.baseCm + w.ridgeCm - baseCm (read by §8.4's caster ceiling and V05's clearance, X20); floors = 1 + max storeyRange(w)[1] over storeyed wings, 0 with none; every other building keeps M11's rule byte for byte (J-V2.78).

V02-0238.statement: Stacks' storeys, rooms, composer, chimneys, shadows: a tier reaches storeyRange's storeys (solid none; storeyed from the storey above the one it stands on; level 0 the lowest storeyed level so a solid pyramid's shrine is storey 0; BCR-V2-33: capacity, Storey.level, Storey.wings read it); each tier's first storey a principal floor of storeyCm.ground (J-V2.85; V03 floorCm reads the tier's ground and upper heights, X18); the composer composes every tier, stair, shrine one to one; tier, shrine, stair admit no dormer; porch only at a storeyed tier 0's main door clamped to the free part and clear of stair 0 (tier admits one, stair none: a solid stack's door takes none); rooms rung emits no hall, gate hall, chapel or tower room; decorative chimneys only on exposed roof; plan chimneys drawn at Chimney.levels' top; V03 plans each storeyed tier and the shrine, landing door on landingSide (X18). One shadow per tier: every tier, stair, shrine its own caster (prism from its own baseCm to its eave with its roof's rise; §8.4 per wing), shadows nest (item 110 (f); T-V2-44).

V02-0239.statement: Stacks' crypts and basements: a stepped building's basement lies under its ground wings (tier 0) whatever storeys they reach (BCR-V2-33); an always-crypt class built in tiers seeds its crypt with tier 0; on wet ground a solid tier 0 >= crypt.clearCm + 100 cm holds its raised crypt inside the platform with no lift (a storeyed annex over the whole inset lifted, V03 §3.7.4); a lower or storeyed tier 0 takes the lift through rebaseStack; where no ground wing is storeyed (V03 ground(b) absent: a solid tier 0 with no storeyed annex) the basement's access is external (BCR-V2-33 extension with §13.2 T29-4, J-A29.25; S23R3-03), its door at V03's basementDoor(b) (tomb door, or the wall side where the stack stands against a retaining wall; a platform crypt entered by the same door at its own floor); a storeyed ground wing beside a solid tier 0 (annex, arena façade ring) joins the basement by its core or trapdoor fallback, never outside (V03 J-V3.88).

V02-0240.statement: Stepped rows (lines 2396-2401; own, calibratable, V11's four anchors; tier 0 size from slotBand: temple and palace carry claimShare (J-V2.87), tiered tower reads its class's tower family budget; reached only by name: V11 specialisations X17, V04 names stepped-monument X19, family op, tiers bend or mutation): stepped-temple (institution; count 3-4/4-5/4-6/5-7; rect 1; insetM 1.5-2.5/1.5-2.5/2-3/2-3.5; solid all 3-4/3.5-4.5/4-5/4.5-6 m; taper .9, flat; top flat .2 shrine .8 at p, shrine 1 else; axial, stairWidthM 2.5-4/3-5/4-6/5-8, grade 1.0-1.2; aspect .65-.85; claimShare .35-.6; shrine floors 1, insetShare .15-.25, roofs hip .4 pyramid .4 gable .2; wingWidthM 5-7; porch none; hearths 0); terraced-palace (count 2-3/2-3/3-4/3-5; rect; insetM 3-5/3-6/4-7/5-8; none, floors 1-2/1-2/2-2/2-3; taper 1, flat; top flat .6 roofed .4; flights 2-3/2-3/2.5-4/3-5, grade .6; aspect 1.15-1.8; claimShare .35-.6; wingWidthM 8-10; porch as hall's; hearths 3/4/5-7/6-10); tiered-tower (detached; count 3/3-4/3-5/4-6; rect .4 octagon .4 round .2; insetM .3-.5/.3-.6/.4-.7/.4-.8; none floors 1; taper .92, pent; roofed 1; internal; aspect 1-1; wingWidthM 4-5; porch .5/.5/0/0/0; hearths 1/1/2/2); stepped-monument (V04 ruins; count 3-5/4-6/5-7/6-8; rect .85 round .15; insetM 1.5-3; solid all 3-5 m; .9 flat; flat .5 shrine .5; axial 3-6, grade .9; aspect .6-.85; heights 350/300 cm; else as stepped-temple).

V02-0241.statement: Stepped load checks (V2 §3.10.7 extended): a row whose families include stepped carries tiers, a row with tiers lists stepped at weight 1; stairs internal never with solid all or lower; flights never with a round or octagon weight above 0; lowerRoof pent only with stairs internal; count[0] >= 2; stairGrade[1] <= stairGradeMax; sealed form none never a row value; a stepped row never read under row, cluster or tents; no row of V2 §3.10.2-§3.10.6 lists stepped (the table half of the no-op pin, T-V2-50).

V02-0242.statement: Stepped mutation: single -> stepped (only source) keeps the main range as tier 0 (W1 anchored test first, drawTiers on siteplan.mutate, layTiers anchored on the range's four corners); a TierFailure leaves the target single (kept range unchanged), reported steppedDegraded; stepped -> single keeps tier 0 as main and subtracts the rest, W5 giving roof and floors (a solid tier 0 becomes storeyed: solid cleared, floors the target's least, recorded as a storey step); stepped -> stepped keeps tiers up to the target's count, subtracts those above (shrine first, then each removed tier's stair with it), adds tiers on top by W6 with MassingRef.stack.insetCm and .grade while ST3's side test passes; every other pair passes through single; inverse steps restore exactly (W9).

V02-0243.statement: A ruin's stepped monument (V04): V04's ruin stage calls drawTiers on its own ruin stream and layTiers alone (never massStepped: no band, ST8, attempts) with the stepped-monument row at the band its ancient-culture row names, in its plan cell's frame, storeys = TierCells.heights (350/300 cm), plinthCm 0, parapetCm 0, scale 1; a TierFailure is V04's (plan cell re-laid smaller, or the monument a mound by persistence order); V04 then decays it (V04's and V11's; X19); the monument is V04's record, not a Building; V02 supplies the one tier construction so ruin and living temple tiers nest by one rule.

V02-0244.statement: Deck buildings (1): every building S11 raises on a deck plot the base offers (item 110 (d): frontage plots along a mole, pier or jetty, quay platform or bridge deck; placed landmarks at a mole head or mid-mole); S11 passes BuildingInput.deck (BCR-V2-34); a raised way's deck carries none (J-V2.71); no deck plot on a ford, drawbridge or unbuilt deck (Bridge kind ford or draw, or deckCm not yet set: offers none; X28 the coherence pass's deck-plot rule); a quay built on the bank is ground (surfaceCm null: deriveBase terrain datum with plinth and skirt, ordinary basement gate, dig floor; keeps kind quay for @deck rows and deck budget); points (5), (6) apply to moles, piers, jetties, bridge decks and quays built over water.

V02-0245.statement: Deck buildings (2) the row: non-landmark reads <key>@deck/<band> else default.<arrangement>@deck/<band>; a landmark reads its class's chain unchanged (mole-head or mid-mole tower the tower family towerHouse; a fort its class's template) with its template's budget and floors (J-V2.69); S11 copies DeckContext.landmark from the deck-plot record's landmark flag (a mole's head and mid-mole slots, a bridge's mid-span slot where the coherence pass adopts one; X28 the producer); the lighthouse islet is land (reached by a causeway: its tower an ordinary tower building with ground datum and basement gate). (3) budget and storeys: non-landmark M10 band = deck budget footprintM2 at the plot's band and deck kind (V11 deck row X16; until it lands deck.fallbackM2 [20,60] m²) x footprintShare_i / count_i x buildingScale per slot, replacing [p10, p90] in slotBand, under cap coverageMax x area(H); M11 clamps every wing's floors to <= maxFloors (fallback deck.fallbackFloors 2; 'small, light', J-V2.67); W5 clamps kept wings likewise. (4) fitting: M2's frontage frame on the deck's way; H inside the deck plot and width (item 110 (f)); row quads pass through.

V02-0246.statement: Deck buildings (5) datum: every wing's baseCm = DeckContext.surfaceCm, no plinth, no skirt (BCR-V2-32); on a bank quay the terrain datum; a change of the deck's height (§4.8's re-base after a terrain stroke, a bridge edit) re-bases the deck's buildings in the same step (their plots in the deck's effective scope, BCR-V2-32). (6) no basement, no crypt, no dig: basement decision gives none on a deck over water (BCR-V2-34); no dig floor; no crypt-bound use ever stands on a deck (J-V2.68 amended): S10b never places on a deck plot a use whose class's crypt column is always or a use a dossier crypt record binds (V04 C4-05) (V11 deckOk per use, X16 extended); a hand placement (T6) of such a use bends to the nearest land plot at the deck's landward end, named (V9C-58 (2)); a designation mutation bringing such a use onto a deck building relocates it to the nearest land building (§10.3). (7) lifecycle: V02 adds nothing to the deck's fate: removing or ruining a deck ruins what stands on it by the base's least-disruption rule (item 110 (d)), each building's fate a record, massing untouched; rebuilding re-offers plots, S11 raises new buildings (new lineages, fresh draws).

V02-0247.statement: @deck rows (own; four anchors; alias of the named row, only named cells overriding): default.row@deck (default.row; back 0, blocks 0, towers 0, turret 0; dormers 0/0/.3/.5; porch 1/0/0/0/0 · .9/.1/0/0/0 · .8/.2/0/0/0 · .7/.3/0/0/0; hearths 1); default.detached@deck, default.compound@deck, default.institution@deck (default.detached; families single 1/single 1/single .85 L .15/single .75 L .25; wing width 3.5-4.5/4-5/4-5.5/4.5-6; range length 4-6/5-7/6-8/6-9; back 0, blocks 0, towers 0, turret 0, dormers 0; porch as default.row@deck; hearths 0/1/1/1); chapel@deck (a bridge chapel; chapel; single 1; width 4.5-5.5; length 6-9; porch .6/0/.4/0/0; cupola 0/0/.1/.2 tip 1; hearths 0); watch-house@deck (a toll house; watch-house; width 3.5-4.5; length 4-6; back 0; hearths 1). Load checks: every @deck row's families in {single, L, row} under the arrangement law; blocks, towers, turret, backRange 0; cupola.chance <= .2.

V02-0248.statement: (a) Retaining walls: the massing reads only H and the datum; S10-S11 level the plot and raise RetainingWalls (item 110 (a)); the site plan keeps H on one level off the wall, so no wing crosses or stands on a wall; a building backing onto one stands off by the template's rear setback which may be 0 (a row built against the terrace wall). The datum reads its own terrace (BCR-V2-32, -42): levelling is a platform datum never a raster write (BCR-V5-30), so every datum sample is levelledGroundCm(doc, key, p) (levelled plot's, block's or ward's platform, else the unlevelled raster), and a wing-vertex sample within terrace.wallBandCm (250 cm, one refined raster cell) of a RetainingWall chain is replaced by the sample at the point moved along the wall's normal toward the wing centroid's side until terrace.wallBandCm from the wall line (no lift toward the terrace above nor sink toward the one below; T-V2-51); a walk-out basement at a low-edge wall is V03's BCR-V3-27 (a); V02 adds no wall rule (J-V2.72).

V02-0249.statement: (b) Raised ways (generated at CITY and METROPOLIS for a ravine or valley, a link between high wards or a water need; declared at TOWN; added or removed by the user, removal holding through regeneration; item 110 (b) as revised ~23:40): V02 composes nothing on a raised part (J-V2.71); piers and the under-deck strip are obstacles the base's plots avoid (S10, S11, V01) so no H meets them; an aqueduct's terminal basin, cistern or fountain house is its class's building (V11 conduit_house); nothing depends on generated vs declared; a user removal frees ground re-plotted by the base's locality; when the user adds one or an epoch raises one (V06) every building whose footprint meets a pier or the strip takes the base's least-disruption fates, its plot removed by V01's V1-3.17.4 add path, same set on every path (an epoch-founded way (V06 §3.19 (7), households displaced with cause clearance) and the same way regenerated stand over the same open ground; J-V2.89: exception for buildings below the deck's underside less raised.clearCm withdrawn); the least soffit over a crossed way is V11's raisedWays.structure.clearanceCm which V01 reads, V02 keeps no clearance; a building inside an arch vault under a raised way (V04 archVault chamber, @underground rows) clamped under the soffit by M11's vaultClamp (X29).

V02-0250.statement: (e) Second known-city fixture (original skeleton at M3a): V02's building bars T-V2-44-T-V2-47 and T-V2-51 run on its stepped temple, its mole with a mid-mole tower and a fort at its mouth, its jetties' deck buildings, its terraced wards and its arena (ovalCourt, laid by massOval from M3a; T-V2-42); its lighthouse islet's tower an ordinary land building; the fixture's own bars V12's (X25); tier construction and deck buildings ship with the base outline builder at M3a (V2 §8.5; BCR-V2-39).

V02-0251.statement: Two new event kinds under T9 shape (L3; no thirteenth tool; a new building still T6 place/build): {t setMassing, building, op MassingOp}, {t setComposition, building, op CompositionOp}. MassingOp: family {family} (re-lay as another family by W1-W9, current wings the seeds, draws on siteplan.mutate); addRange {from PointsForm two points (centre line, item 101 (i)), widthCm?, floors?, role? range/cross/service}; reshapeRange {wing key, ends?, widthCm?}; addTower {from one point centre, radiusCm?, shape? round/square/octagon, turret?, floors?}; moveTower {wing, at, radiusCm?, shape? (ring re-made at same centre and radius)}; addBlock {wing host, at on its ridge, lengthCm?, depthCm?}; backRange {on, lengthCm?, widthCm?, side? left/right}; removeWing {wing}. CompositionOp: dormers {wing, eave, count, widthCm?, kind?}; porch {kind or none, widthCm?, depthCm?, entrance? (an Entrance ordinal: the secondary porch at that side, rear or yard entrance, hood or none)}; room {role hall/gatehall/chapel, on, fromCm?, toCm? (extent along host's ridge)}.

V02-0252.statement: Storeys and roofs of one wing are setAttr on wings/<key>/heights/floors and wings/<key>/roof (kind, pitch, high), addressed by key (BCR-V2-12); a lock on wings/<key> (attribute-level, §7.2) holds that wing against every mutation, re-derivation and edit of another wing; re-rolls the base's regenerate with rung wings or rooms; the massing's re-roll is New random on the plot; draws (J-V2.18): geometric ops draw nothing (omitted defaults the row's deterministic central value), the family op draws on siteplan.mutate (replay exact).

V02-0253.statement: setMassing step 1 new wing set: family: V2 §3.9's steps recorded as MutationSteps in EditBase.mutations; a family op into or out of stepped also writes the use's stepped specialisation in the same undo group (SCC-28); addRange: two snapped points the centre line; width given or the row's middle; an end within w of another range's long side ends on it (butt, abutting); an end within w/2 of another's free end turned by more than 2° mitres with it; role range unless given; floors given or the main wing's; roof by the role's default; reshapeRange: ends and width move, abutting ranges re-trimmed, a block on it re-split (M7); addTower: centre, radius and shape given or row's middle, floors one above the tallest wing it meets; moveTower: same tests at the new centre, new shape re-makes the ring (stored plan's room and stair re-cut by the plan rung); addBlock: M7 at the point; backRange: M9 on or off with sizes and side; removeWing: key never re-used; a removed block's host pieces re-join keeping the lowest key; removing the main wing passes the role to the longest remaining range (ties by key). Every writer re-sorts into canonical order and rewrites segments before the dry run.

V02-0254.statement: setMassing bends, never refusals (item 101 R2; J-V2.79), each named with its closest alternatives: removeWing of the last wing bends to T6's remove of the building, one undoable event (bend.building.remove); reshapeRange on a row quad (party walls the plot's, J-V2.13): ends' moves along the frontage bend to the plot edit moving that party-wall line (plot moveVertex on the frontage vertex, neighbour's quad re-clipped by S11, one event; bend.row.plotLine; a lock on the neighbour's quad or plot refused with the lock named), its width re-cuts the quad's rear chain at the new depth inside the plot and back region (the quad an edited pinned wing); removeWing on a non-last row quad removes it (a gap, neighbours' party-wall ends reclassed as gables, remaining wing takes main); a family op unreachable or infeasible bends to the reachable feasible family nearest (fewest growth-lattice steps, ties by target weight) naming the least plot the asked family needs and offering join (bend.family.nearest).

V02-0255.statement: setMassing dry run (overlay §7.1): usable region = plot less the plot's other buildings' footprints buffered by attractCm (build to the plot line, never over a neighbour, passage's other side or way); checks M13's (tiling apart from towers, containment, ring rules, minEdge) and M8 (ii)-(v) for towers; M10's budget not applied to a hand edit (capacity follows the shell); failing op bent to the nearest lawful one named in one line: range crossing the region clipped; tower through a wing moved outward by the least distance passing (iii); overlapping range trimmed to a butt joint; wing below 4 m² or side below minEdge grown about its centre line (width first to 2 m, then length until 4 m²) inside the region (bend.wing.grow); op beyond the plot clipped and offers join; an op on or moving a locked wing refused with the lock named (with a dossier fact the only refusals); the dry run lists from V03's plan query every stored-plan room, edited opening and furnished room the op would orphan (V03 3.11, 4.3) with §7.3's orphan actions.

V02-0256.statement: setMassing commit: S11's operator on the plot with the new wings fixed (moveFootprint's path, §2.6 rule 5): footprint re-inserted with other buildings fixed, deriveBase, entrance set re-derived (edited entrance kept, §7.2; entrance hint re-read), basement re-derived unless edited keeping an always-class crypt with no condition and a basement-class church's while in the church family (cathedral by the no-refusal ladder and wet-ground lift), yard partition re-fitted (new hole typed court, BCR-V2-24), capacity re-read with excess re-homed by §4.7's overflow pass, first carry; a stored composition re-matched by key (W8) and a stored plan re-cut inside the event by V03 3.11 around its edited parts; unstored wings rung marked stale. Locality (§7.3 item 1): the plot (faces and buildings), the passage a wing spans, buildings receiving re-homed households (T-V2-19). Undo keeps former wings, Building.massing, nextWingKey, stored composition and everything S11's re-fit changed (§7.4 S11 rows), restoring exactly incl. a re-homed household's former building.

V02-0257.statement: setComposition: the first on a building stores its composition (current derived composition with the op applied) as Building.composition, record edited (§2.6 rule for the first composition or plan edit). dormers: count clamped to the eave's bays (facadeBays) and named; row marked edited (fixed input to V03's dormers). porch: a kind whose space fails bent to the nearest feasible kind, named; with entrance sets or removes the secondary porch (a hood; other kinds bent to hood, named). room: hall, gate hall or chapel on or off with extent along its host's ridge, bent to the nearest lawful extent (V2 §3.13 (3)) and named; marked edited (fixed ring for the plan rung) and kept while its host keeps its key; a stored plan re-cut inside the event by V03 3.11, dry run listing orphaned stored-plan rooms, edited openings, furnished rooms (V03 3.11, 4.3); turning a room on where no host admits it bends (J-V2.79): a gate hall without a gate range becomes a gate passage through the main-entrance wing eave to eave at the entrance's offset, the row's central gateHallM wide, ends arches to street and yard (bend.room.passage); a hall or chapel goes to the main wing else the largest storeyed wing (chapel at its east end); on a building whose wings are all solid the op first turns the tiers above tier 0 storeyed (tiers solid lower) then places the room in the lowest, both named. Scope the building; undo restores the former composition or removes it when this event stored it (J-P48 (5)); stored rooms and plan points carried by carryWings; composed wings and towers follow base wings by key.

V02-0258.statement: setMassing lifecycle row: create T9 shape handles and family picker at the building band, clerk's shape call, skeleton line; read Building.wings (roles, keys), Building.massing, nextWingKey; persist log, wings model data; regenerate: edited wings are a fixed input to every later S11 run on the plot (§7.2 implicitly pinned), carried by carryWings under warps, a designation mutation keeps an edited wing (base step 4); undo: former wings, massing reference and S11's re-fit; migrate by building address and wing key (BCR-V2-11 anchor), an op naming a missing key orphaned and reported, a family op whose family a later grammar retires maps through the grammar's migration row. setComposition row: create T9 shape at the building band, clerk; read stored dormer rows, porch, secondary porch, edited rooms; persist log, the first one stores the composition; regenerate fixed input to the wings rung (dormers, porches) and rooms rung (edited room), re-matched by key when wings change (W8), an edited dormer row a fixed input to the plan rung; undo the former composition or none; migrate by building address and wing key (secondary porch by entrance ordinal).

V02-0259.statement: Orphans (§7.3 orphan table; J-P48): an edited dormer row whose eave changed length by more than ± 10 %, an edited room whose host key left, a secondary porch whose entrance left, each with two actions: re-attach (dormer row to the same eave of the same key with count clamped to the new bays; room to its role's lawful host with extent clamped; porch to the nearest side, rear or yard entrance) and discard (derived value returns); nothing orphaned dropped silently. Controls (§7.8; BCR-V2-30): fantasyShapes a registered control (output metric the share of fantasy families among composed buildings, consuming stage S11, locality re-derive from S11 with fate report first, continuity discrete off/on, documentation V2 §3.3, advanced panel); the FM building look is a style choice listed for V09's style panel, changes no model byte.

V02-0260.statement: Canvas handles (V09 draws; contract): at the building band each range two centre-line end handles and a width handle (reshapeRange); each tower centre and radius handles (moveTower) and a shape chip (moveTower {shape}); each wing a storey stepper and roof-kind chip (setAttr); each eave a dormer stepper (setComposition dormers); main entrance a porch chip and every side, rear or yard entrance a hood toggle (setComposition porch); with the plan shown, hall, gate hall, chapel an on/off chip and two extent handles (setComposition room); a family strip showing feasible families as dry-run ghosts of setMassing family, one tap committing; every drag previews its dry run live inside the plot (§14 interaction contract) and commits one event on release. The clerk (V10) calls the same operations through the tool API (§11.2) ('make the manor an H' = setMassing {family H}; 'a round tower on the north-east corner' = addTower; 'two dormers on the street side' = setComposition dormers on the main wing's street eave) and reads massing and composition through the reader under §9.2 (every building's mass public, J-A30.83). A skeleton file carries these events as ordered declarations (§11.1): build then setMassing lines re-created exactly by the creation prefix's fold (§4.1's read-ahead reads no stage-3 declaration ahead; massing runs at its plot's S11, declared ops apply at their log positions).

V02-0261.statement: WhyProvider for kind building (J-V2.51) at paths massing, wings/<key>, composition, filling V10's WhyAnswer with no new field: facts massing/family, massing/row, manifested band and value, drift bounds, fantasyShapes, massing/segments, massing/axis with MassingRef.low, each wing's role, floors, roof; alternatives as fact rows massing/alternatives/<family> = renormalised weight among M3's feasible families or 'infeasible: <failed test>', wings/<key>/rejected/<i> = the M8 test a rejected tower failed, composition/porch/d and /feasible, composition/dormers/<key>/<eave>/dropped = obstacle; each tier derived with row the composition.json slice; cause S11's massing (step S11, rule V2 §3.5, chance massing with creation index), the setMassing event (seq), or the mutation's W1 draw or kept seeds (chance siteplan.mutate); sunlit choice names sunBias and factors; alternatives recomputed by re-running M3 and M5/M8 tests without advancing any stream so an untouched building's answer equals its recorded draws (T-V2-43); 'why no crypt / why this crypt' is V03's and V04's provider.

V02-0262.statement: MassingOp gains tiers {count?, insetCm?, top? flat/shrine/roofed, stairs? axial/flights/internal/none, stairWidthCm?, shape? rect/round/octagon, lowerRoof? flat/pent, solid? all/lower/none, shrineInsetShare?, centre?, radiusCm?}: re-lays a stepped building's stack on its tier 0 (layTiers anchored mode); on any other building it first bends to family stepped. No refusal but a lock or dossier fact (J-V2.79): every limit of a stack, deck or row is a bend named in one line with closest alternatives (words V09's X21 and the clerk's X22 under V2 §1b's ids); bends draw nothing, each one undoable event, undo restores the leaf digest exactly.

V02-0263.statement: tiers op on a non-stepped building bends to setMassing {family stepped} followed in the same event by the op's values (bend.tiers.stepped: 'Made it a stepped building first'), V2 §3.15.5's anchored single -> stepped on the main range drawing on siteplan.mutate as a family op; where W1's anchored test fails bend.family.nearest applies. Stepped specialisation (SCC-28; J-V2.94): this bend and a setMassing {family stepped} write in the same undo group (EditBase.group) an editTable row op on the use's siting.declared use: row (V11 §4.2) setting specialisation to V11 §3.24.3's row id for the use's culture and class where one exists, else stepped_temple for the worship family, terraced_palace for palace, tiered_tower for tower_house, mage_tower or watchtower, no cell otherwise (own plan rows stay); so Use.specialisation, the heights row it names (stepped-shrine) and V03's plan rows follow, held and exempt from chance and cap; a family op from stepped on a use holding a stepped specialisation writes specialisation none the same way; undo removes the row op; a skeleton replays both lines.

V02-0264.statement: tiers op on a stepped building re-runs layTiers anchored on tier 0 with MassingRef.stack and the op's values, no draw; an omitted value keeps the stored one (count = tiers standing; step stack.insetCm; grade stack.grade; top; stair form; stair width current; shape, skirt, solid mode, shrine inset as laid); a new tier takes row central values (floors = max(1, round-half-up(central(tierFloors) x taper^k)) or height central(solidHeightM) x taper^k to the cm); keys: a kept tier keeps its key and its ring and heights exactly where step, shape and stair form are unchanged (else ring re-inset, key and heights kept); a stair keeps its key across a change of stair form while its tier stands (ring re-laid) and is removed with its tier or under internal or none; tiers above the new count removed with their stairs and everything on them (keys retired); new tiers and stairs take keys from nextWingKey; the shrine comes and goes with top.

V02-0265.statement: tiers fields and bends: count above what fits bent to the most that fits; insetCm leaving no second tier to the largest lawful step (bend.tiers.count, bend.tiers.step); stairs flights on round or octagonal bends to axial (bend.tiers.axial); internal over a solid tier 0 bends to none where every tier is solid, else axial (bend.tiers.none, bend.tiers.axial); none over a storeyed tier 0 bends to internal (bend.tiers.internal); where the asked form's reserve does not fit in front of tier 0 inside the plot the forms are tried in J-V2.74's order, none fitting keeps the current form named with the depth needed; none (sealed, lawful wherever tier 0 is solid): ST3 uses d on every side, ST5 lays no stair, ST6 skips the chain check, stairChain empty, landingSide null, storeyed tier or shrine reached by nothing (W_TIER_UNREACHED) named; shape re-lays tier 0 as the named shape inscribed in its ring's bounding rectangle (round/octagon at that rectangle's inradius, rect the rectangle), stack re-inset; centre and radiusCm (round or octagonal tier 0): re-laid regular ring clipped by the least move to the plot region, re-inset; lowerRoof pent bends to flat unless the stair form is internal or none (bend.stack.roof); a stair form turned axial or flights on a pent stack turns its lower roofs flat in the same event, named; solid all/lower/none: a tier turning storeyed takes the row's central floors, one turning solid keeps its eaveCm (less parapet) as its height; unlawful stair forms bend as above; shrineInsetShare re-lays the shrine (ST4 tests; no fit -> top flat, named).

V02-0266.statement: A tier's height: setAttr(wings/<key>/heights/floors) on a storeyed tier or the shrine, setAttr(.../eaveCm) on a solid tier; in the same event rebaseStack re-bases every wing standing on it directly or through the chain and each stair whose rise changed is re-laid (ST5, width kept): where the terrace no longer holds the run at the stack's grade the grade steepens up to stairGradeMax, beyond that the height is bent to the most the terrace allows, named; setAttr(.../baseCm) on a wing with on bends to the same change in its support's height (solid support eaveCm by the difference; storeyed support floors by round-half-up(difference / storeyCm.upper), zero result a no-op named) then the rules above (bend.stack.base); a user's baseCm on a ground wing kept (J-DET-24) carrying the stack; from M3a to M6c the base's setAttr of a wing's heights (index = key) does the same through the base outline builder (BCR-V2-39). Roofs on a stack (bend.stack.roof): a lower tier to flat or its shape's pent kind (hip rect, pyramid octagon, cone round; pent only under internal or none); top tier among flat, hip (rect), pyramid (octagon), cone (round), another kind bends to its shape's; a stair to shed; the shrine among TierCells.shrine.roofs else the first; MassingRef.stack.lowerRoof stays the laid default a later re-lay applies.

V02-0267.statement: Other setMassing ops on a stepped building: reshapeRange on tier 0 re-insets the whole stack (keys kept; a tier no longer fitting removed with its stair and everything on it, named); removeWing on tier k >= 1 removes it, its stair (to = tier k), every wing standing on it and every higher tier with its stair; removeWing on tier 0 removes the stack (tier 0, every stair and wing on it), ground wings added beside it stay (longest takes main, family single, stack cleared), none left -> bend.building.remove; removeWing on a stair bends to tiers {stairs internal} where tier 0 is storeyed, else tiers {stairs none} (bend.tiers.internal, bend.tiers.none); addRange, addTower, backRange admitted as ground wings (no on; bend.stack.groundWing) laid by V2 §4.2's rules outside tier 0's ring, every stair's ring and stair 0's approach strip (reserve width, landingM deep in front of stair 0's foot; internal: landingM in front of the main entrance; none: no strip), moved away by the least distance; a range ending within w of tier 0's side abuts it; a back range takes tier 0 as host (M9 rear side); a tower passes M8 (ii)-(v) with tier 0 as host, clear of wings on tier 0, stairs and strip, its eave raised above tier 0's roof in its ring; addBlock bends to addRange of the block's size on the ground beside tier 0; M13's pairing covers tier 0, stair 0 and added wings; ST6 nesting unchanged; family runs V2 §3.15.5's rows.

V02-0268.statement: Deck buildings in edits: every op works as on any building inside the deck plot (region inside the deck's width); a floors value above the deck's maxFloors bent to it, named ('a deck carries at most n storeys'), for setAttr of floors and addRange's floors alike (J-V2.70); M10's budget not applied to hand edits; a family stepped op on a deck building bends to single (bend.deck.single: 'A bridge carries small, light buildings', deck kind named); a hand placement of a crypt-bound use on a deck plot bends to the landward land plot. Locality, undo, lifecycle as V2 §4.2 (4)-(5): scope the plot (bend.row.plotLine adds the neighbour's plot, one event); a stack's re-base and re-lay stay inside the building; undo keeps former wings, nextWingKey, MassingRef.stack; V2 §4.4's setMassing row covers the tiers op and its bends; a skeleton carries tiers lines (a bent line replays to the same bend).

V02-0269.statement: Stack editing surfaces: clerk ('give the temple five tiers' = tiers {count 5}; 'a shrine on top' = tiers {top shrine}; 'stairs along the faces' = tiers {stairs flights}; 'seal it' = tiers {stairs none}; 'make it round' = tiers {shape round}; 'skirt roofs on every tier' = tiers {lowerRoof pent}; 'one more storey on the second terrace' = setAttr floors; V10 X22); V09 draws at the building band a tier stepper, a step handle on tier 1's front face, stair-form, top-form, shape, skirt and solid chips, a shrine-inset handle, centre and radius handles on a round or octagonal tier 0, a storey or height stepper per tier (X21); WhyProvider adds massing/stack/* (shape, row's stair form and the one laid, lowerRoof, top, insetCm, grade, truncated, drawn count, derived aspect), wings/<key>/on, wings/<key>/solid, massing/stairSteep, each bend taken (massing/bend/<id>), and for a deck building massing/deck (deck kind, host, budget band, maxFloors, whether fallback constants were read), each with its composition.json or V11 slice, no new WhyAnswer field.

V02-0270.statement: What each band draws: city: the massing as masses (§8.5 (2) closing per block; a court wider than the closing's 1.5 px stays open (a yard part, ground at this band); towers and cross-wings show in silhouette; no roof lines), model eager; district: footprints with outlines and entrance ticks (base) and the massing's roofscape (ridges, hips, valleys, walls, tower roofs and spires, cupola) by the style's construction; an arcade wing's ground-storey outline dashed; no dormers or porches; model drawn lazily per tile; neighbourhood: plus, where the wings rung is current or stored, dormers, entrance gable, porch and §8.10's decorative chimneys at façade-bay lines (hearths of them; none once the plan exists, J-A28.85); change marker on a stale building (§8.5); model + cache; building: full detail and the plan storey by storey (V03), other storeys' wing outlines faded (base). Under a Works (item 67) wings at stage heights with §8.2 states rows: wallsRising no roofscape facet; roofFramed roofscape lines through §8.2's frame program without fill; decayed or ruined (roof none) no facet, walls by states rows (ruined landmark included); a stack under Works takes stage heights from BCR-V2-40's heightsAt (stack order, a solid wing by courses of storeyCm.upper, no wing drawn or cast before its support reaches its eave, each stair rising with the tier whose top it reaches, demolition in reverse; reaches V06's Works, X23); roof none takes no dormer, porch or cupola; condition (worn, neglected) and material texture and colour only (item 19).

V02-0271.statement: roofscape(building, composition?): planar pairwise non-overlapping facets covering the footprint (and a porch outside), derived at read in the tile worker (float64, renderer CPU reference) and generation worker (exports), stores and draws nothing. (1) Ends (resolveEnds): each ridged wing's two ends (sides 1 and 3 for ridgeAxis 0, 2 and 4 for 1) classed in order: open if a tower ring covers it; party on a plot party-wall edge; mitre if shared vertex for vertex with another wing's end; along another wing Y's side (butt): wall when Y.eaveCm >= X.ridgeCm - 10, gable when X.ridgeCm > Y.ridgeCm + 10, else valley; a free end hip on a hip roof, gable otherwise; a block's side partly shared with a piece's end classed on the shared part. (2) Ridge lines: base ridge (rect: ends' midpoints; quad: arc-length midpoints of its ridgeAxis chains), hip pulls the end inward by WingRoleRow.hipInset x span (0.5 ranges; a block's FM entry 0.25 until calibrated keeps a ridge half its short side, never a pyramid), collapsing to the centre only when the wing is no longer than 2 x hipInset x span; valley extends it into Y by e = (X.ridgeCm - Y.eaveCm) / Y.slope; gable, party, mitre, wall, open leave it at the end's midpoint (mitre: the path vertex).

V02-0272.statement: roofscape (3) facets per wing: gable/hip two long facets eave to ridge plus a hip triangle at each hip end; a valley end's facets continue into Y up to the valley lines (plan projections of X's facet planes meeting Y's near facet plane, clipped to Y's footprint; where X's eave is below Y's the valley starts where X's facet reaches Y's eave height); shed one facet low eave to high side; pyramid and cone one triangle per ring edge to the apex over the centroid; pent band facets (J-V2.75): for a pent wing x and wing y on it (concentric, equal insets, same vertex count) one planar facet per side i from x's side at x.eaveCm to y's side i at x.ridgeCm, neighbours sharing the vertex-to-vertex edge as hip line, round or octagonal per edge, nothing inside y's ring (ridgeCm = eaveCm + p x d meets the tier above's wall); a pent-kind roof with nothing on it laid as the top's roof (ST4); tent as a cone at its pitch; spire a cone or pyramid at spire pitch; flat one facet at eave height with an inner parapet line where parapetCm > 0; dome four latitude bands of planar quads (triangles at apex), rise = ring mean radius x domeRise (1.0), band rings scaled by cos of latitude (15°, 37.5°, 60°, 82.5° by dmath); plain (F-SKELETON downgrade) one flat facet, no lines; none no facet (excluded from tiling, drawn by states rows); skeleton the base's validated straight-skeleton faces (§3.8) with plain downgrade; cupola a small solid at its range's ridge midpoint (square plan side 0.3 x width, drum 0.25 x that side, dome/tip (cone rise 2 x half side)/pyramid) extra facets part cupola, never in Heights; every facet vertex carries z (cm above the lowest baseCm).

V02-0273.statement: roofscape chimneys (§8.6, §8.10): a decorative chimney (no plan) at its host point on its host facet; a plan chimney (§2.6 Chimney) drawn on the roof or terrace facet over Chimney.column of the wing holding storey Chimney.levels[1] whose ring contains the column (a lower tier's stack carried up rises from the top of the stack, V3C-68 (2)); a chimney whose column lies inside the ring of a wing standing on that wing (stored plan not yet re-cut) is not drawn, reported chimneyCovered until the plan re-derives. (4) Occlusion: each valley region removed from Y's facets; each tower ring removed from every other facet (M11 guarantees the tower's eave is above); each ring of a wing standing on another removed from its support's facets; a dormer's plan rectangle removed from its host facet and replaced by its own facets (dormer/wallGable two facets from its front edge to a short ridge perpendicular to the host's, depthShare up the slope; hoist with a flat front; entranceGable two facets whose ridge runs to the host's ridge); porches add facets (hood one thin facet; gabled, twoStorey two facets with ridge square to the wall; halfRound half-cone triangles per arc segment to the apex on the wall line; recessed none, a notch line in the eave); result tiles footprint ∪ porches less roof-none wings (T-V2-9); cupola facets over it, excluded from tiling. (5) Lines: ridges, hips, valleys, eaves, wall end lines, tower seams (every other ring vertex's edge for a cone with >= 16 sides, every edge for a pyramid). (6) Order: porch, wing (stack order), dormer, tower facets, then lines.

V02-0274.statement: §8.4 (a)'s surface layer takes roofs from these facets (light pass on true roof planes and cones). Shadow casters are the base wings' prisms (ring from baseCm to eave plus roof rise over its ring; a tower's cone or spire only over its own ring), model heights, so no shadow of the model's masses depends on a click (J-V2.22); also item 102's epoch casters, never generation-time. Surface-layer shading of porches, dormers and cupola appears with their drawing: view only, no digest, no caster.

V02-0275.statement: StyleSheet.roofConstruction gains 'roofscape', the default construction of every shipped family from stage 3's landing; older constructions remain for the parity presets (MFCG, FTG keep the base massing and their constructions). Paint programs added: roofscape(tone twoTone/mono/facet) fills every facet in the roof role (twoTone by faceLight per facet for lit; mono one tone with light-pass shading for ink; facet per-facet diffuse-and-specular of the reference look for the FM building band, §8.4 (h), P24), then step-5 lines in ink at ½ the building outline weight (ridges, seams) and ⅓ (hips, valleys); dormer and porch via the same tone rule outlined at ½; towerRoof a cone's facets with seam lines, a pyramid's with hips, a spire's at its pitch; the cupola through towerRoof at ½ weight.

V02-0276.statement: Roof decorations (§8.10 rows, view data, keyed by render key): sails (windmill's four sails on its tower roof turned to the settlement's prevailing wind where the site states one, else +y); smokeStack (V2 §3.14.6's decorative stacks); only in the FM building look stepStones (stone path from the main door to the frame's access side, stones 0.5-0.8 m at 1 m pitch) and wallGrass (grass tufts at re-entrant corners); with the FM look's per-building roof hue (weathering on hue at w 0.15, §8.2) and cone facets doubled for drawing only. V01's NG draw-style bars: from M6a the NG parity sheet keeps fakeGablePerWing; at M6b re-measured on roofscape and switched when they pass else kept, reported (the one sentence V01's V1-7 and X14 share). hatch(ridge or eave, pitch, taper) in §8.2: the hatched family's hatch program is V01's (V1-5.1.2) run per roofscape facet; the FM look hatches parallel to the eave at a fixed paper pitch (0.9 px at 1x, ours). The lit family's roof tint by band (item 19) and the material's pattern apply per facet, never changing a facet (J-A19.42); the contrast matrix is unchanged (roof role pairs are the building role's).

V02-0277.statement: Labels: stage 3 adds no LabelTable row and no S13b candidate (landmark point label at its footprint, address kept); room labels the base's (§8.5, from the plan rung); hovering a wing at the district band and finer names its role from the naming slice building.wingRole (one entry per WingRole in V11's naming tables: 'the main range', 'the gate range', 'a cross-wing', 'a pavilion', 'a rear range', 'a service range', 'a tower', 'a stair turret', 'a part', 'a shelter'; role id the fallback) and the building's name through the reader (§11.2) under knownTo (§9.2); nothing concealed; ovalCourt solid ranges hover 'the seating' and gate passage wings 'a gate passage' (two entries X6 adds, keyed by family and solid flag); stacks add 'a tier', 'the shrine', 'a stair'.

V02-0278.statement: Exports: JSON per building a massing block (family, row, grammar, entrance hint, segments, low, cupola; each wing's key, role, kind, ring, heights, roof, arcade) and where the wings rung is current or stored a composition block with state (row, grammar, composed wings with base and dormer rows with derived positions, towers base, porch and secondary porch with derived rings, courts derived rings, rooms); round-trips (T-V2-24). SVG at district band and finer (§11.1 grouping, S23-08): roofscape facets in sem.building.roof, .dormer, .porch, .tower, .cupola (by RoofFacet.part), step-5 lines in sem.building.roofline, each group one compound path per (semantic, district) in step-6 order; metadata map carries each facet's subpath range to wing:<building>/<key> (porch to its building, cupola to its range's wing); no per-building group, no data-wing attribute (§12.7 element budgets); city band nothing new. glTF/OBJ: roofs from facets, towers ring prisms with cone, pyramid or spire, cupola small mesh; arcade ground storey open (piers four corner prisms, walls from first storey); with compositions dormers and porches small meshes; extras carry key and role; option compositions asDrawn (default: current or stored), derive (compose() for every building of the scope first in the pool under V2 §6's export budget), none. CityJSON 2.0: LoD2.2 RoofSurface per facet, WallSurface from wing prisms, dormers and porches as surfaces when exported; plat:role and plat:key in the Plat extension (plat.ext.json). GeoJSON optional wings layer (strict and metric): one Polygon per base wing with key, role, floors, eaveCm, ridgeCm, roof, building; building features carry onDeck, deck and a stepped building's tiers (f item 447), wings layer repeats none (S23-32). VTT unchanged at the ground scene; a tower's ring part of the footprint walls; storey scenes V03's.

V02-0279.statement: Stacks on the map: city band the footprint (tier 0 ∪ stair 0 and ground wings) as a mass; district band and finer the roofscape with stack occlusion and order (terraces flat facets with parapet lines, pent skirts band facets meeting the tier above's wall, top's roof or shrine's, each stair's shed facet by stairFlight; a sealed stack draws no stair; chimneys only on exposed roof); an ovalCourt draws its façade ring's flat roofs with parapet lines and its seating ring's shed facets falling toward the floor, drawn as a court (yard part); neighbourhood and building bands V2 §5.1's, the plan per storeyed tier (V03). stairFlight (paint program, BCR-V2-15): facet filled by the roofscape tone rule (slope lit by faceLight), tread lines across perpendicular to the climb by stairTreads (n - 1 lines at goingCm from the foot) in ink at ⅓ of the building outline weight, stopping short of each side by a tenth of the flight's width; below 2 px of plan per tread omitted (reads as a ramp). Surface layer and shadows: each wing's facets enter §8.4's surface layer at true heights; casters the wings' prisms from their own baseCm kept current by rebaseStack (each tier's shadow on the terrace or ground below); under a Works BCR-V2-40's stage heights. Per-wing constructions (parity sheets and the base builder's drawing from M3a until the roofscape lands at M6a): a wing on another drawn after it, its ring clipping the lower roof, a stair's shed with treads (BCR-V2-36).

V02-0280.statement: Stack exports: JSON each wing's on and solid, the massing block's stack, and for a deck building a derived deck block (kind, host) read from its plot at export; glTF/OBJ each wing extruded from its own baseCm, a solid tier a closed prism, each stair a stepped solid of stairTreads' n risers (k-th top at floor(k x rise / n)) and treads of goingCm, the head tread taking the remainder; CityJSON 2.0 tier 0 the Building, each tier above and the shrine a BuildingPart with LoD2.2 surfaces (terrace a RoofSurface, walls WallSurfaces from the part's own base), each stair a BuildingInstallation (outer stair stepped by stairTreads) with plat:role stair (J-V2.77); GeoJSON wings layer on, solid, baseCm per wing; VTT ground scene walls from the footprint, a stair's outer sides not walls; a deck building exports as any building with the deck's baseCm.

V02-0281.statement: Budgets PLAUSIBLE until measured; building counts §1.1's (TOWN 1 200-1 500, CITY 4 500-6 000, METROPOLIS 12 000-15 000 at rung targets; about 30 000-36 000 at the 120 000 cap); assumed mix §2.6's cost note (about 55 % row quads, 25 % single ranges, 18 % tiled multi-wing, 2 % with towers).

V02-0282.statement: Massing cost per building (median, PLAUSIBLE): row 1-3 µs; single 3-6 µs; tiled families (L, T, H, U, cross, rectCourt, gridWalk) with blocks 15-40 µs; plotRing and fantasy 30-60 µs; with towers or turret + 20-60 µs; an F-MASSING attempt x (1 + attempts). Bars (stage-3 intake, BCR-V2-22): town-wide median <= 10 µs per building (base admission bound; estimate ≈ 3 µs); composed classes (family not row, single, shelter, baseOutline) median <= 60 µs, p99 <= 250 µs; mean over all <= 12 µs; S11's §12.4 row re-declared by the measured difference (estimate mean + 6 µs). V02-0519.statement: massing: stage 3's plan of a building's base wings (outline() M0-M14), recorded as BaseWing[] and Building.massing.

V02-0520.statement: composition: the lazy composer result (wings and rooms rungs) over a massing; stored only when edited.

V02-0521.statement: base wing (BaseWing) and composed wing (Wing.base): the massing's wing record keyed by wing key, and the composition's wing that names its base wing and carries nothing of its own.

V02-0522.statement: wing role (WingRole): main, range, part, tier, shrine, stair (and the seating, gate passage of ovalCourt).

V02-0523.statement: wing key: a wing's stable ordinal, never changed or re-used; edit paths and streams name the wing by it (Building.nextWingKey).

V02-0524.statement: MassingRef: Building.massing (family, row, grammar, entrance hint, segments, stack).

V02-0525.statement: massing family (MassingFamilyId): the vocabulary of plans (single, L, T, H, U, rectCourt, the five FM families, stepped, ovalCourt, ...).

V02-0526.statement: resolution chain: the order in which a building finds its CompositionRow (designation template's composition, classFamily, templateFamily, default).

V02-0527.statement: slotBand: the size band of a stepped slot from the slot hint and claim share.

V02-0528.statement: facadeBays(wing, side, bayM): the bays of a wing side (integer), in @plat/plots.

V02-0529.statement: roofscape: the building-wide roof plan from all wings at once (ends, valleys, walls, towers resolved; planar non-overlapping facets).

V02-0530.statement: stack, tier, stack order: wings standing on others (BaseWing.on), tier 0 the ground wings, stack order supports before their stacked wings.

V02-0531.statement: solid wing (BaseWing.solid) and sealed stack: a wing with floors 0 (no storey, room or capacity); a stack with stair form none.

V02-0532.statement: stack helpers deckLevel, storeyRange, stairChain, landingSide: derived-at-read functions in @plat/plots.

V02-0533.statement: approach strip: stair 0's derived approach region (stair reserve width, landingM deep in front of stair 0's foot; under internal in front of the main entrance; none under none), stated in V2 §4.6.

V02-0534.statement: rebaseStack(b, ground): the one building datum pass for a stacked building.

V02-0535.statement: cryptSeedWings(b) (seed wings) and the raised/half-sunk crypt: the wings a derived crypt is seeded under; the wet-ground forms of the no-refusal crypt ladder.

V02-0536.statement: DeckContext and deck plot: a plot built on a deck host (mole, pier, quay platform, bridge) and its context (host, kind, surface height, landmark).

V02-0537.statement: bend: the named alternative outcome replacing every structural refusal (item 101 R2), with a bend id.

V02-0538.statement: fantasyShapes: the model control admitting Fantasy Manor's families among composed buildings.

V02-0539.statement: identity composition: the composer's fallback (composed wings and towers one to one, no dormer, porch or room).

V02-0540.statement: B-MASS and the free-frame harness: V02's bench fixture set and the FM parity harness (plat/bench/fm-parity/).
